targets.old_statement: A driver passing a bicyclist keeps at least three feet of clearance, while a bicyclist passing parked cars keeps at least three feet from their doors.
targets.statement: A motorist passing a bicyclist should keep at least three feet of clearance until safely past, while opening a vehicle door unexpectedly in a way that creates a hazard for moving traffic or bicyclists is a traffic violation.

correction.corrected_statement: A driver passing a bicyclist must keep at least three feet of space until safely past.
correction.note: Removed parked-car door clause not on cited page.

targets.old_statement: A pedestrian should wait for the next cycle when the green has been showing for a while, while a pedestrian must never step out at all when vehicles are approaching close by.
targets.statement: A pedestrian must cross only within crosswalks rather than jaywalking, while a pedestrian facing a green light that has been showing for some time should wait for the green signal on the next cycle before starting across.

correction.corrected_statement: A pedestrian should wait for the next green cycle when the green light has been showing for some time.
correction.note: Removed close-vehicles clause not on cited page.
